'''''Persicaria orientalis''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Polygonaceae]],<ref name=POWO_60455314-2/> known as '''kiss-me-over-the-garden-gate''' and '''princess-feather'''.<ref name="FNA">{{citation |first1=Harold R. |last1=Hinds |first2=Craig C. |last2=Freeman |contribution=Persicaria orientalis |contribution-url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242100104 |access-date=2019-05-04 |name-list-style=amp |editor-last=Flora of North America Editorial Committee <!--|year=1982–2021 -->|title=Flora of North America ''(online)'' |publisher=eFloras.org }}
</ref> It was first described,  as ''Polygonum orientale'', by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753. It was transferred to the genus ''[[Persicaria]]'' by [[Édouard Spach]] in 1841.<ref name=IPNI_60455314-2/> Its native distribution is unclear.<ref name=GRIN_409766/> As of April 2023, Kew's Plants of The World Online lists its native distribution as ranging from the Russian far east to Indochina, Malesia and Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Persicaria orientalis (L.) Spach {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60455314-2 |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref> It is widely cultivated and naturalized.<ref name=GRIN_409766/>
